images.caption: Figure 1:VFlashis a generalist decoding framework for fast, accurate visual planning across Physical AI tasks such as robotics and autonomous driving. By aligning prediction blocks with the known structure of visual primitives, it enables parallel decoding of common structured outputs such as bounding boxes, variable-length 2D/3D trajectories, and dense point motion, while retaining verified speculative decoding for text and sub-task plans. Compared with autoregressive (AR) decoding, VFlash improves accuracy on 3D robot trajectory planning while substantially reducing decoding latency across NVIDIA platforms, including Jetson Thor, DGX Spark, and H100.

Figure 2:FPD design.A primitive-start token triggers a prediction block layout determined by the primitive type and the preceding tool calling. By adapting the prediction block to each primitive’s structure, VFlash supports different spatial formats and lengths without requiring token-level agreement with the VLM.
